rv.q: Mindplay is captivating and visually stunning, from the shadowplay that enhances certain magic tricks to the projections DePonto uses to illustrate his stories.
While it falters in the narrative department, it’s one of the best magic shows you may ever see.
DePonto delivers his framing with mindblowing expertise, rhythm, and charm, filling our heads with memorable amazing moments with the psychological tricks he has charmingly up his sleeve.
A warm presence, DePonto gently coaxes folks to the stage, which is furnished with a desk that has a gooseneck lamp, a holder with pens and pencils, and a telephone.
I can promise that, as in any good 'magic' show, the happily baffled audience walks out wondering, how the hell did he do that?

cn.t: DePonto's interactive mentalism show proves engaging and occasionally touching, blending mind-reading tricks with personal storytelling about memory. Critics find it entertaining and well-crafted, though some note it's more confounding than illuminating.
